topic.title: Why did Britain hide a power station inside a mountain?

title: Why did Britain hide a power station inside a mountain?
description:
Why is there a power station hidden deep inside a mountain in Wales?
Dinorwig, inside Elidir Fawr in Snowdonia, waits in the dark for one moment every night.
Sources: Wikipedia, Dinorwig Power Station (Nov 2026).
Maps simplified. Borders as recognised by the country each video is about.
cta: Kettle or mountain: which surprised you more? Comment

lines.text: Why did Britain hide a whole power station inside a mountain in Wales?
Under the grass of Elidir Fawr, in Snowdonia, there is a cave 51 m high, with giant machines spinning in the dark.
On top sits one lake, Marchlyn Mawr. At its foot sits another, Llyn Peris. And tunnels run through the rock between them.
At night, while Britain sleeps and power is cheap, the machines pump water uphill, from the low lake into the high one.
So why pump a lake uphill? Because now the whole mountain is a battery, full of water, waiting.
And what it waits for is a kettle. When a big final ends on TV, millions of people get up and switch one on, all at once.
And then? The gates open. The water falls through the mountain, the machines spin, and out come 1,800 megawatts.
It keeps that going for 6 hours, until the top lake is nearly empty.
It opened in 1984, built inside the rock, so the national park above still looks wild.
But its real secret is speed: with its machines already spinning, it reaches full power in about 16 seconds, long before a single kettle boils.
Kettle or mountain: which one surprised you more? Tell me in the comments. And next time you boil one, think of that mountain in Wales.

notes: 5 figures computed from inputs; 5 cross-checked against closed-form formulas.

All 5 facts confirmed on en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinorwig_Power_Station: six 300 MW units = 1,800 MW installed; zero to 1,800 MW in ~16 s with all six units synchronised and spinning (script says 'about' and 'machines already spinning'); up to six hours at full flow; cavern 51 m tall; opened/commissioned 1984 (infobox). Verify list ok: TV pickup up to 2,800 MW from millions of kettles; Marchlyn Mawr 636 m upper, Llyn Peris ~100 m lower; no specific match named. Also confirmed: inside Elidir Fawr to preserve Snowdonia National Park, off-peak/night pumping of cheap energy. Description ends with the channel disclaimer. Notes: 'keeps that going for 6 hours' is the article's 'up to six hours'; max sustained supply is 1,728 MW vs 1,800 MW installed (the 16 s figure is stated as 1,800 MW, so acceptable).

Re-review after fixes: lakes is now a side cut-through of Elidir Fawr (new picture, LLYN PERIS clear of captions at 15s), hidden beat shows OPENED 1984 plaque and the grassed-over hall outline, cavern is a torn rock opening with housed turbines, thumbnail at 9s shows the lit hall; all on the map but one beat, disclaimer on the last frames, loop and pick-one ending fine.
